ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on two sides of $\triangle MON$, segments OA and OB are intercepted respectively, such that $OA=OB$; arcs are drawn with point A and B as centers and the length of OA as the radius, intersecting at point C; lines AC, BC, AB, and OC are drawn, intersecting at point D. If $AB=4\,cm$ and the area of quadrilateral OACB is $16\,cm^2$. Point E is the midpoint of CB, and line DE is drawn. What is the length of segment DE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Based on the given information, we know that $AC=BC=OA$,\\
$\because$ $OA=OB$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=BC=OA=OB$,\\
$\therefore$ the quadrilateral OACB is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ $OD=\frac{1}{2}OC$, $BD=\frac{1}{2}AB=2\text{cm}$, $AB\perp OC$,\\
$\because$ $AB=4\text{cm}$, the area of the quadrilateral OACB is $16\text{cm}^2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}AB\times OC=16$,\\
$\therefore$ $OC=8\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ $OD=\frac{1}{2}OC=4\text{cm}$,\\
$\because$ in $\triangle ODB$, by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $OB^2=OD^2+BD^2$,\\
$\therefore$ $OB=\sqrt{OD^2+BD^2}=\sqrt{4^2+2^2}=2\sqrt{5}\text{cm}$,\\
$\because$ point E is the midpoint of CB, point D is the midpoint of OC,\\
$\therefore$ DE is the midline of $\triangle OBC$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=\frac{1}{2}OB=\boxed{\sqrt{5}}\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, two rays OM and ON are emitted from point O, point A is on ray OM, and point B is on ray ON; A, B, C, O are connected to form quadrilateral OACB. Line segment AB intersects OC at point D, point E is located on CB and is connected with D, and in the figure construction traces of making arcs near A and B and then intersecting at C can also be seen. Reasoning: From the construction it can be known that AC=OA, BC=OA; it is also known that OA=OB, so AC=BC=OA=OB, the four sides of quadrilateral OACB are equal, and it is a rhombus. The diagonals AB and OC of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other and bisect each other, therefore D is the midpoint of the two diagonals, BD=AB/2=2 cm. The area of a rhombus is equal to half the product of the two diagonals, so 16=(AB×OC)/2=(4×OC)/2, obtaining OC=8 cm, therefore OD=OC/2=4 cm. In right triangle ODB, OB=sqrt(OD^2+BD^2)=sqrt(4^2+2^2)=2sqrt(5) cm. Because D is the midpoint of OC and E is the midpoint of CB, DE is the midline of triangle OCB, DE=OB/2=sqrt(5) cm.
